In [[differential geometry]], the '''Ooguri–Vafa metric''' is a four-dimensional [[Hyperkähler metric]]. The Ooguri–Vafa metric is named after [[Hirosi Ooguri]] and [[Cumrun Vafa]], who [[Species description|first described]] it in 1996 using the [[Gibbons–Hawking ansatz]]. Another construction was given by [[Davide Gaiotto]], [[Greg Moore (physicist)|Gregory Moore]] and [[Andrew Neitzke]] in 2008.

== Definition ==
The Ooguri–Vafa metric is defined on the four-dimensional total spaces of principal U(1)-bundles over open subsets of the  three-dimensional [[euclidean space]] <math>\mathbb{R}^3</math>.<ref>Lorenzo, p. 1</ref> In particular the whole space results in <math>\mathbb{R}^3\times S^1</math>.<ref>Gaiotto, Moore & Neitzke 2008, p. 7</ref>

Define the elliptical fibers <math>\tau(z)=\frac{1}{2\pi i}\log(z)</math> with <math>\tau_1=\operatorname{Re}(\tau(z))</math> and <math>\tau_2=\operatorname{Im}(\tau(z))</math> and let <math>\lambda</math> be the [[Coupling constant#String theory|string coupling constant]]. Further define the scaled spatial coordinate
:<math>\mathbf{y}=\left(x,\frac{z}{\lambda},\frac{\bar{z}}{\lambda}\right)</math>.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Summing up D-Instantons|first1=Hirosi |last1=Ooguri |first2=Cumrun |last2=Vafa |journal=Phys. Rev. Lett.|volume=77|number=16 |date=1996|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.77.3296|arxiv=hep-th/9608079|url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.77.3296 |pages=3}}</ref>

The metric of Ooguri and Vafa has the form<ref>{{cite journal |title=Summing up D-Instantons|first1=Hirosi |last1=Ooguri |first2=Cumrun |last2=Vafa |journal=Phys. Rev. Latt |pages=4}}</ref>
:<math>ds^2=\lambda^2[V^{-1}(dt-\mathbf{A}\cdot d\mathbf{y})^2+V d\mathbf{y}^2]</math>
where <math>\mathbf{A}=(A_x,A_z,A_{\bar{z}})</math> and
:<math>A_x=-\tau_1=\frac{i}{4\pi}\log\left(\frac{z}{\bar{z}}\right),\quad A_z=0,\quad A_{\bar{z}}=0</math>
and <math>V</math> is a potential which gets modified from the form <math>V=\tau_2=\frac{1}{4\pi}\log\left(\frac{1}{z\bar{z}}\right)</math>. 

=== Requirements for the potential ===
There are 5 requirements for the potential <math>V</math>:<ref>{{cite journal |title=Summing up D-Instantons|first1=Hirosi |last1=Ooguri |first2=Cumrun |last2=Vafa |journal=Phys. Rev. Lett. |volume = 77 |number = 16 |date= 1996|doi= 10.1103/PhysRevLett.77.3296 | arxiv = hep-th/9608079 |url= https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.77.3296 |pages = 4-5}}</ref>
* <math>V</math> should be a function of only <math>x</math> and <math>|z|</math>, i.e. <math>V(x,|z|)</math> for <math>|z|=\sqrt{z\bar{z}}</math>.
* For the metric to be a hyperkähler metric, the following conditions must be met:
:<math>V^{-1}\Delta V = 0,\quad\text{and}\quad \nabla V = \nabla \times \mathbf{A}</math>
:where the [[differential operator]] <math>\Delta</math> is defined as follows:
:<math>\Delta :=\partial_x^2+4\lambda^2\partial_z\bar{\partial}_{\bar{z}}.</math>
* If <math>|z|\to \infty</math> then one obtains the classical potential defined above:
:<math>V(x,|z|)\to \frac{1}{4\pi}\log\left(\frac{1}{z\bar{z}}\right)</math>
* The metric should be periodic, but not translation-invariant, in the <math>x</math>-direction with period <math>1</math>, i.e. <math>V(x,|z|)=V(x+1,|z|)</math>.
* The singularities of <math>V</math> can be removed by a suitable coordinate transformation.

There exists a unique solution which satisfies all these conditions<ref>{{cite journal |title=Summing up D-Instantons |first1=Hirosi |last1=Ooguri |first2=Cumrun |last2=Vafa |journal=Phys. Rev. Lett. |volume=77 |number=16 |date=1996 |publisher=American Physical Society |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.77.3296 |arxiv=hep-th/9608079 |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.77.3296 |pages=5}}</ref>
:<math>V(x,|z|)=\frac{1}{4\pi}\sum\limits_{n=-\infty}^{\infty}\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{(x-n)^2+z\bar{z}/\lambda^2}}-\frac{1}{|n|}\right)+C</math>
for a constant <math>C</math>. Using Poisson's formula on gets
:<math>V(x,|z|)=\frac{1}{4\pi}\log\left(\frac{\mu^2}{z\bar{z}}\right)+\sum\limits_{m\neq 0}\frac{1}{2\pi}e^{2\pi i mx}K_0\left(2\pi\frac{|mz|}{\lambda}\right)</math>
where <math>\mu</math> is a constant and <math>K_0</math> is the modified [[Bessel function]].
